headline: November ferrous scrap settled $20–30 a ton higher, Chicago included
detail: US mills paid about $20–30 per gross ton more than in October, with Chicago shredded up about $30 and busheling about $20. Strong mill order books and thin scrap flows support prices going into December.

headline: LME copper falls to a four-month low near $13,210
detail: Three-month copper dropped as much as 1.4% Monday, about 10% below September's record, on Fed rate-hike bets, worries about AI spending and soft China data. Firm Chinese import buying may limit the slide.

headline: Dollar hits its highest since April 2025 on December Fed-hike bets
detail: The dollar index rose to about 103.5 after hot October inflation and hawkish Fed talk, with futures pricing a quarter-point hike on Dec 9. A stronger dollar and higher rates weigh on copper, aluminum and precious metals.

headline: Nucor lifts its hot-rolled coil price to $1,295 a ton, 17th straight weekly rise
detail: Nucor added $15 a short ton with lead times at 3–5 weeks. Firm sheet prices keep mills buying prime and shredded scrap.

headline: China iron ore futures drop to their lowest since 2022
detail: Dalian iron ore fell toward 650 yuan a ton as China's October steel output slipped 1.6% and supply from Guinea's Simandou mine grows. Weak Chinese steel demand pushes cheap steel abroad and caps world steel and scrap prices.

headline: US mill output jumps 6% in a week; utilization 81.7%
detail: AISI says US raw steel output was 1.886 million tons in the week to Nov 14, up 9.1% from a year ago. Busy mills mean steady demand for scrap.

headline: Platinum and palladium fall about 3% as the dollar climbs
detail: Platinum dropped about 3% to near $1,446 an ounce and palladium about 3% to near $971 Monday along with gold and silver. Lower PGM prices cut catalytic converter values.

headline: CFTC chairman orders a review of the aluminum Midwest premium
detail: The regulator's chairman asked staff to study aluminum pricing, including the Midwest premium, and reform options. Can makers say the premium inflates costs; any change could affect how US aluminum and aluminum scrap are priced.

headline: LME aluminum cash premium hits its widest since 1990
detail: Metal booked to leave LME warehouses jumped about 21%, pushing cash aluminum well above three-month prices. Near-term physical supply is tight even while futures stay soft.

headline: COMEX copper stocks hit a record as the US premium over LME nearly vanishes
detail: COMEX stocks reached about 732,000 tonnes, and a refined-copper tariff looks less likely after the midterms. The premium that topped $700 in August is almost gone, removing support under US copper and copper scrap.

headline: China's October factory output, retail sales and investment all miss forecasts
detail: Industrial output grew 4.8% versus 5.3% expected and retail sales just 0.4%. A slowing China weakens demand for copper, steel and aluminum.

headline: Trump and Xi to meet Thursday at APEC in Shenzhen
detail: The leaders plan a meeting and lunch Nov 19, with China's pause on an extra 24% tariff extended to Jan 10. A tariff-cut deal or new friction could swing copper and broader risk appetite.

headline: Canada threatens to sue Stellantis over moving Jeep Compass work to Illinois
detail: Ottawa gave Stellantis 30 days to respond after it shifted planned Compass production from Ontario to Illinois. More Illinois assembly would mean more Midwest stamping scrap and steel demand.

headline: US ferrous scrap exports fell 14% in September
detail: Exports were about 938,000 tonnes, down from August but up 7% on the year, with shipments to Turkey down nearly a fifth. Weaker export pull leaves more scrap at home, though tight domestic supply has cushioned it.

headline: Gold sinks to its lowest in over a year and silver drops nearly 4%
detail: Spot gold touched about $3,832 before ending near $3,859, and silver fell to about $47. Rate-hike bets and a strong dollar are driving precious metals lower.

headline: Strike at Teck's Highland Valley copper mine enters a fourth week
detail: More than 1,200 workers are out in British Columbia and picketing has disrupted concentrate shipments in North Vancouver. It could trim fourth-quarter copper supply.

headline: Indonesia's president wants 70% of mining returns to go to the state
detail: Prabowo gave no details or timeline, but Indonesian mining shares fell. Indonesia supplies about two-thirds of the world's nickel and hosts the Grasberg copper mine, so it could tighten supply.

headline: 30-year mortgage rate climbs to about 7.3%
detail: The average 30-year fixed rate rose about 0.3 point in a week as Treasury yields rose. Higher borrowing costs hurt homebuilding and demand for copper wire, plumbing and steel.

headline: Copper miners sell off: Freeport down nearly 7%
detail: Freeport and Southern Copper both fell more than 6% as the 10-year Treasury yield hit about 5.14%. Investors are pulling money out of copper.

headline: Markets fully price a December rate hike; some talk of a half point
detail: Futures now fully price a Dec 9 hike after hot October inflation, and a Fed governor had floated a 50-point move in that case. Faster tightening is a headwind for industrial demand and metal prices.

headline: China's home-price slide eases but the property slump goes on
detail: Big-city prices were nearly flat on the year, but only 14 of 70 cities rose month to month. Weak property keeps Chinese steel and copper demand soft.

headline: Chinese platinum and palladium futures slide on weak buying
detail: Guangzhou platinum futures fell 3.3% and palladium 1.9% as Chinese buyers held back with enough stock on hand. Weak Asian demand adds pressure on PGM and converter values.

headline: Gold steadies in Asia ahead of Fed minutes
detail: Gold rose about 0.5% to near $3,874 early Tuesday and silver about 1% to $47.50, both still near one-year lows. Wednesday's Fed minutes are the next test.

headline: Canada says it could turn to Chinese automakers if US trade talks fail
detail: Prime Minister Carney raised the option ahead of meeting Xi in Shenzhen. It adds uncertainty to North American auto output and its steel and aluminum supply chains.

headline: Tariffs look hard to repeal even after the Democrats' midterm win
detail: A presidential veto makes repeal difficult, so the Section 232 metal tariffs that prop up US steel and aluminum prices are likely to stay for now.
